source.title: Aligned but Fragile: Enhancing LLM Safety Robustness via Zeroth-Order Optimization
source.authors: Zhi-Hao Liu; Yi-Fan Wu; Jian Lou; Dingzirui Wang; Yuxi Zhou; Yu-Ke Hu

page_placements.theme: Compression, pruning and noise have conditional safety effects

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests safety behavior under parameter and activation perturbations and evaluates a ZO robustness-refinement method. It does not test any listed claim version: it does not measure fine-tuning on harmful or benign examples, token-position KL, compliant prefills or jailbreak/decoding bypasses, localization of ordinary safety behavior in a few parameters, or token-depth training.
record.gate_note: The paper cites harmful/benign fine-tuning and token-depth work as related work, but reports no results testing those claims. Its own safety-rate results concern injected noise, quantization, and robustness refinement, so they are recorded under fits_no_version. Layer-sensitivity scores and comparisons among the paper's selection methods are not catalogued as separate results here.
record.test_reason: The paper's own results measure how ASR changes under quantization, weight noise and activation noise, and how ZO refinement after FO safety training changes that ASR. It runs no harmful or benign fine-tuning attack, no per-token KL, no prefill, suffix or decoding bypass, and no token-depth training. Its layer sensitivity scores rank layers by robustness to perturbation; they do not test whether safety itself sits in a few weights. Qi et al. (both originals) are cited only in related work, so the relation is cites_only, not discusses.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is essentially correct. The authors conclude that standard safety alignment stays fragile under quantization, weight noise and activation noise. They conclude that a few ZO steps after FO alignment improve robustness at modest cost, and that robustness-aware layer selection beats SNIP and WANDA selection.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses CB-Safety for FO safety alignment followed by ZO robustness refinement, and evaluates injected parameter/activation perturbations and quantization. It does not use the harmful- or benign-fine-tuning, token-position KL, or opening-token bypass procedures in the cited original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by model, perturbation type and level, and ASR measure. The paper reports different results across quantization, weight-noise, and activation-noise conditions, and between Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Qwen2-7B-Instruct.

fits_no_version.finding: On Llama-3-8B-Instruct, quantization, Gaussian weight noise and activation noise each raise ASR on all three judges, more so at stronger levels. The largest rise is LlamaGuard3 ASR from 0.0833 to 0.6267 at activation noise α=0.12.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety-aligned models lose safety under generic post-alignment weight, activation or quantization perturbations.

fits_no_version.finding: On Llama, 10 ZO steps after 100 FO steps mostly give small further ASR reductions under perturbation (about 0.01–0.07). A few cells are unchanged or slightly up.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Brief zeroth-order refinement after safety training modestly improves the robustness of refusal to parameter and activation perturbations.

fits_no_version.finding: On Qwen2-7B-Instruct, SFT+ZO versus SFT changes are small, mostly decreases, and some are unchanged. Under W4A4 the model degenerates (PPL >2800), so ASR there is uninformative.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Effects of ZO robustness refinement depend on model and perturbation.

record.problems: The reported ASR results provide no error bars, confidence intervals, or p-values. The main text's detailed perturbation table is for one model, with additional Qwen results in the appendix; the excerpt does not state the number of evaluation prompts for these experiments.
record.rows_left_out: The 60-row limit is reached. Omitted results include Table 2 Stage I FO-alignment outcomes; additional ZO results in Table 4 and Table 6; unselected Qwen perturbation conditions and most of the full strategy-comparison results in Tables 7 and 9. These concern perturbation robustness rather than the listed claim versions; rows were retained for the main Llama perturbation outcomes, selected Llama FO+ZO comparisons, and representative Qwen results.

untested.parts: All: no benign fine-tuning evaluated for harmful compliance. The FO/SFT stage is safety training on CB-Safety and lowers ASR.
All: no per-token KL between aligned and base models.
All: no prefill, suffix or decoding bypass. The AdvBench refusal-prefix measure is used only as a judge.
All: the layer scores measure sensitivity to noise or quantization, not where safety is localized.
All: ZO refinement targets robustness to parameter and activation perturbations, not safety depth across token positions.

record.verdict_notes: This is the right call for T6/cites_only. The main data quality issue is Table 8 (Qwen): the arrows do not match the sign of the numeric changes, and the reader copied that inconsistency into the states. No row should link to any version.

versions.untested_parts: No harmful-example fine-tuning or harmful compliance after such fine-tuning is tested.
No benign-data fine-tuning or resulting harmful compliance is tested.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL measurement is reported.
No compliant-start prefilling, adversarial suffix, or decoding-change bypass is tested.
Layer sensitivity to perturbations is studied, but the paper does not test whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
The paper does not test whether data or training objectives produce token-level shallowness.
ZO refinement is tested for robustness to perturbations, not for spreading safety beyond the first response tokens or for the persistence of such deepening.

relation.reason: The introduction and related work cite token-depth alignment and harmful or benign fine-tuning findings as background; the study neither tests those findings nor uses them as its method.

tranche.reason: The study measures perturbation robustness and optimizer-based refinement, without testing or using any listed version. Layer sensitivity does not establish concentration in a small set of weights or ranks.

source_check.notes: All listed values and baselines match Table 1. All three safety measures use the non-hash HarmBench split; AdvBench denotes a refusal-prefix measure. The stronger-perturbation trend has an exception: HarmBench ASR falls from 0.2567 at alpha=0.10 to 0.2333 at alpha=0.12.
